haiku-low.q1: After step 4, once the Message Service's store transaction commits, the sender gets an ack containing {msg_id, seq} via the gateway. It confirms the message was stored.
haiku-low.q2: The sender sees an error and nothing is published, so no one receives it. The retry must carry the same msg_id so the store returns the original seq instead of inserting again.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 seconds without a heartbeat. Heartbeats every 10 s reset the 30 s TTL, so the key expires and the user counts as offline.
haiku-low.q4: The gateway's 5 s timer expires and a push is requested. The Offline Inbox entry stays until the client acks that msg_id.
haiku-low.q5: It is logged and not retried. The Offline Inbox entry is left untouched.
haiku-low.q6: After fetching bodies by msg_id, messages are sent per conversation in ascending seq order. Clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
haiku-low.q7: The message and its outbox row are committed in one transaction. If the store crashes after commit, the outbox row remains and the relay still publishes the event.
haiku-low.q8: In the Presence Registry, an in-memory key-value store mapping user_id to gateway node. The 30 s TTL expires the key when heartbeats stop.
haiku-low.q9: The worker sends the message to gateway G's delivery queue, and G writes it to the socket. A client ack of msg_id within 5 s confirms receipt and deletes the Inbox entry.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox, as a per-user pending entry written for each recipient before any delivery attempt. An entry is removed when the client acks that msg_id, or it expires after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: It reads the user's pending entries from the Offline Inbox, then fetches the message bodies by msg_id from the Message Store.
haiku-low.q12: The event is not acked, so the bus redelivers it and another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id).

sonnet.q1: After steps 1-4: once the Message Store transaction (message insert + outbox row) commits, the sender gets ack {msg_id, seq}. It tells them the message is durably stored with its sequence number; it does not wait for fan-out or delivery.
sonnet.q2: Sender gets an error; no outbox row exists so no fan-out and nobody receives it. The retry must carry the same client-generated msg_id; the store then returns the original seq instead of inserting again.
sonnet.q3: After 30 s without a heartbeat (heartbeats every 10 s reset the 30 s TTL), the presence key expires and the user counts as offline.
sonnet.q4: A push is requested; the Offline Inbox entry stays (it is deleted only when the client acks), so the message can still be delivered on reconnect.
sonnet.q5: It is logged and not retried; the Inbox entry is untouched.
sonnet.q6: Per conversation in ascending seq order. Duplicates are dropped by msg_id (and live messages arriving during reconnect are placed by seq).
sonnet.q7: The message insert and outbox row are committed in one transaction, so the outbox row exists once committed; the Outbox Relay publishes it independently of the service, so fan-out still happens. The client's retry gets the original ack.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry, an in-memory key-value store mapping user_id to gateway node. The 30 s TTL expires the key when heartbeats stop.
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker looks up the user in Presence Registry, finds node G, and sends the message to G's delivery queue; G writes it to the WebSocket and starts a 5 s timer. The client acking the msg_id within 5 s confirms arrival (and deletes the Inbox entry).
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox, as per-user pending entries (pointers, not bodies) written for every recipient before any delivery attempt. An entry is removed only when the client acks that msg_id (live or after reconnect); entries also expire after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: It reads the user's pending entries from the Offline Inbox, then fetches the message bodies by msg_id from the Message Store.
sonnet.q12: The event was not acked, so the bus redelivers it and another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id) and clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
